level1.text: The attenuation coefficient of a telecommunications fibre is $0.18\,\text{dB/km}$. What is the attenuation of a fibre $50\,\text{km}$ long, in decibels?
The power of light is $2.0\,\text{mW}$ at the start of a fibre and $0.50\,\text{mW}$ at the end. What is the attenuation of the fibre in decibels?

Assume that the eddy currents in the base of a pan on an induction hob can be described as one current loop with a resistance of $0.010\,\Omega$, in which flows an alternating current with an effective value of $400\,\text{A}$. At what power do the eddy currents change electrical energy into internal energy of the base? Give the answer in kilowatts.

The magnetic field of a wireless charger is uniform at the receiver coil of a phone and perpendicular to the plane of the coil, and the peak value of the magnetic flux density is $0.50\,\text{mT}$. The area of one turn of the coil is $12\,\text{cm}^2$. What is the peak value of the flux through one turn? Give the answer in microwebers.

Assume that a wireless charger takes a power of $10.0\,\text{W}$ from the wall socket and a power of $7.2\,\text{W}$ is transferred to the battery of the phone. What is the efficiency of the charging? Give the answer as a percentage.

On an induction hob the base of the pan heats up, but the glass plate above the coil does not heat up by itself, even though the magnetic field of the coil passes through it. Which of the following explains this best?
level1.answer: Glass does not conduct electricity, so no eddy currents arise in it to heat it.

choices.text: Glass blocks the magnetic field, so the coil does not produce a changing flux at the glass plate.
choices.feedback: Glass does not block a magnetic field. The field passes through the glass and produces eddy currents in the base of the pan. The reason is that no electric current can flow in glass.

choices.text: The melting point of glass is so high that eddy currents cannot raise its temperature.
choices.feedback: The melting point does not decide whether eddy currents arise in the glass. If a current flowed in the glass, it would heat up. What matters is that glass does not conduct electricity.

choices.text: Glass does not conduct electricity, so no eddy currents arise in it to heat it.
choices.feedback: Correct: the changing flux induces a voltage in the glass, but in a material that does not conduct electricity it does not produce a current. Without eddy currents there is no electrical energy changing into internal energy in a resistance, and the base of the pan heats up instead of the glass.

choices.text: According to Lenz’s law, the eddy currents that arise in glass cancel each other, so no heating takes place.
choices.feedback: Lenz’s law does not cancel eddy currents; it gives their direction: they oppose the change of flux. No currents arise in glass at all, because it does not conduct electricity.

level1.text: A power of $4.0\,\text{mW}$ is fed into the start of a fibre. The attenuation coefficient of the fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$ and its length is $45\,\text{km}$. What is the power at the end of the fibre? Give the answer in milliwatts.
The attenuation coefficient of a fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$. Over what distance does the power of light in the fibre halve?

level2.text: The receiver coil of a phone has $10$ turns. The frequency of the charger is $140\,\text{kHz}$, and the magnetic flux through one turn varies sinusoidally with a peak value of $0.40\,\mu\text{Wb}$. What is the peak value of the voltage induced in the coil?

The transmitter of a fibre link feeds a power of $1.0\,\text{mW}$ into the fibre, and the receiver detects the pulses when the power is at least $1.0\,\mu\text{W}$. The attenuation coefficient of the fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$. What is the greatest possible length of the link without an amplifier? Ignore the attenuation of the splices.

The cooking zone of an induction hob takes a power of $2.0\,\text{kW}$ from the mains. Assume that $85\,\%$ of the power is transferred to the water in the pan. The pan contains $1.5\,\text{kg}$ of water at a temperature of $15\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How long does it take to heat the water to the boiling point, $100\,{}^\circ\text{C}$? The specific heat capacity of water is $4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}}$. Give the answer in minutes.

In a measurement (Ravenscraft, OneZero, 2020) charging a phone from empty to full took $14.26\,\text{Wh}$ of energy from the wall socket with a cable charger and $21.01\,\text{Wh}$ with a charging pad. Assume that the phone is charged from empty to full once a day for a year ($365$ days). How much more energy does the charging pad use in a year than the cable charger? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

The efficiency of a wireless charger was measured at different distances between the charger and the receiver coil of a phone. The measurements are example data.

Draw a graph with the efficiency on the vertical axis and the distance on the horizontal axis, and join the points with a smooth curve. Determine the distance at which the efficiency falls to $50\,\%$. You can read the value from the graph or interpolate linearly between two measurement points.

Write the distance in millimetres in the answer box.

level2.text:
The attenuation of a fibre was studied by measuring the power that came through sections of fibre of different lengths. In every measurement a power $P_0 = 800\,\mu\text{W}$ was fed into the start of the fibre. The measurements are example data.

For each length, calculate the attenuation $A = 10\,\text{dB} \cdot \lg \dfrac{P_0}{P}$ and draw a graph with $A$ on the vertical axis and the length $L$ on the horizontal axis. Fit to the points a straight line through the origin: the line goes through the origin because a fibre of zero length has no attenuation. The slope of the line is the attenuation coefficient of the fibre.

Write the attenuation coefficient in the unit $\text{dB/km}$ in the answer box.

data.caption: Power that came through the fibre (example data)

level2.text:
A student solves a problem: “The attenuation of a fibre is $20\,\text{dB}$. Decibels are like percentages, so the power decreases by $20\,\%$ and $80\,\%$ of the transmitted power arrives.”

a) Explain what is wrong in the student’s reasoning.

b) What percentage of the transmitted power arrives when the attenuation is $20\,\text{dB}$?

Write the result of part b in the answer box.

The server of an online game is connected to the player's home by an optical fibre link whose length is, as an example value, $1200\,\text{km}$. The refractive index of the fibre core is $1.47$, and the speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Light travels in the fibre almost parallel to the axis, and delays in the equipment are not taken into account.

The player's command travels as a light pulse to the server, and the reply returns along the same fibre. What is the order of magnitude of this round-trip time?

choices.feedback: Here the length has been substituted as the number of kilometres, $1200$, although the speed is in metres per second. The length is converted into metres before dividing, $1200\,\text{km} = 1.2 \cdot 10^6\,\text{m}$.
Here the length has been written as $1.2 \cdot 10^5\,\text{m}$. Kilo means a thousand, so $1200\,\text{km} = 1200 \cdot 10^3\,\text{m}$, that is $1.2 \cdot 10^6\,\text{m}$.
Correct: light travels in the fibre at the speed $c : n = 2.04 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$ and covers the distance $2.4 \cdot 10^6\,\text{m}$, so the time is about $11.8\,\text{ms}$.

Here the speed of light has been taken as the number $300\,000$, which is the speed in kilometres per second, although the length has been substituted in metres. The length and the speed must be in the same units.

level2.text: The figure shows the same wireless charger at two distances: the phone is $3\,\text{mm}$ and $6\,\text{mm}$ from the charger. The field lines are drawn at equal flux steps, so the number of lines passing through the receiver coil is proportional to the flux $\Phi_0$. The peak voltage of the receiver coil at a distance of $3\,\text{mm}$ is $4.2\,\text{V}$, and the frequency stays the same. Use the lines of the figure to calculate the peak voltage at a distance of $6\,\text{mm}$. Give the answer in volts.

The figure shows the power of light passing through one fibre as a percentage of the transmitted power, as a function of the length of the fibre. The fibre is the same along its whole length. Read from the graph the length at which the power has halved, and use it to calculate the attenuation coefficient of the fibre. What percentage of the transmitted power arrives when the length of the same fibre is $35\,\text{km}$? Give the answer as a percentage.

level3.text:
The submarine cable C-Lion1 is $1172\,\text{km}$ long (Cinia, 2016).

Assume that the attenuation coefficient of its fibres is $0.18\,\text{dB/km}$ and that the attenuation of one section of fibre may be at most $20\,\text{dB}$ before an optical amplifier restores the power of the light. The sections are of equal length, and the amplifiers are between the sections; the transmitter and the receiver are at the ends of the cable.

What is the smallest number of amplifiers the cable must have?

The coil of an induction hob at a frequency of $25\,\text{kHz}$ produces in the base of a pan a sinusoidally varying magnetic field whose magnetic flux density has a peak value of $4.0\,\text{mT}$.

Assume that the field is uniform and perpendicular to the base, that the eddy currents in the base can be described as one loop with a radius of $8.0\,\text{cm}$ and a resistance of $0.050\,\Omega$, and that the magnetic field of the eddy current itself is ignored.

At what mean power does the base heat up? Give the answer in kilowatts.

The transmitter of a fibre link feeds a power of $1.0\,\text{mW}$ into the fibre, and the receiver needs a power of at least $10\,\mu\text{W}$. The attenuation coefficient of the fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$, and the link has four splices, each of which attenuates by $0.50\,\text{dB}$.

The refractive index of the glass of the fibre is $1.47$.

How long does it take a light pulse to travel from end to end of the longest possible link, when the pulse travels along the axis of the fibre? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in milliseconds.

The receiver coil of a wireless charger has $N = 15$ turns, and the frequency of the charger is $f = 130\,\text{kHz}$. At different distances $d$ from the charger, the peak value $e_0$ of the voltage induced in the coil was measured. The measurements are example data.

The phone starts to charge when the peak value of the voltage is at least $1.0\,\text{V}$. The manufacturer is considering lowering the frequency of the charger to $100\,\text{kHz}$ so that the flux at each distance stays the same.

a) Calculate the peak value $\Phi_0$ of the flux through one turn, in microwebers, for each distance in the table.

b) Calculate the peak value of the flux at which the voltage is exactly $1.0\,\text{V}$ at the frequency $100\,\text{kHz}$. Using linear interpolation, determine the greatest distance at which charging still works at the new frequency.

c) Explain why the working distance becomes shorter even though the field of the charger does not change, and suggest one change to the receiver coil that would restore the distance.

Write the distance of part b in millimetres in the answer box.

data.caption: Voltage of the coil as a function of distance (example data)

level3.text:
An induction hob operates at the frequency $f = 30\,\text{kHz}$. The coil produces at the base of the pan a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to the base and varies sinusoidally, with a peak magnetic flux density of $B_0 = 3.0\,\text{mT}$.

Assume that the eddy currents in the base can be described as one loop with a radius of $r = 9.0\,\text{cm}$, and that the magnetic field of the eddy current itself is ignored. The resistances of the loops in the bases of three pans are in the table.

a) Calculate the mean power at which the base of each pan heats up.

b) At what frequency would the coil make the base of pan C heat up at the same power as the base of pan A heats up at $30\,\text{kHz}$, when the peak value of the flux density stays the same? Justify how the power depends on the frequency.

c) Give one reason why the base of a real pan heats up at a different power from that given by the model.

Write the frequency of part b in kilohertz in the answer box.
